title: Manager: one loose-ends task, and the rules that stop loose ends becoming tasks
item: Fix the small problems the reviews of tasks 57, 37, 61 and 58 left in the manager, and change the rules so that a task's own small problems are fixed before it merges and the advisor reviews drafts and does not write them
motivation: In two days agents created 18 tasks. Two were built as their own task, 5 were dropped (4 folded back into the task that produced them) and the rest wait. Each manager task merged on 2026-11-17 left one more 'small fixes' task behind (59, 62, 64, 65), and the advisor spent 122,189 and 87,348 agent tokens writing pass lines for two of them, one of which grew a new mechanism nobody had asked for. The owner's rulings of 2026-11-17: fix it here; an agent may create a task in one case only; the advisor is a reviewer, not an author.
notes: This task replaces tasks 59, 62, 64 and 65, which are Dropped as folded in. Their files stay as the lists of what to fix; read all four, with tasks/advice/064-1.md and 065-1.md. NEW RULES (owner, 2026-11-17). (a) An agent creates a task in one case only: a problem that existed before the task's branch and lies outside its change. Still at most one Proposed task per task run. (b) Fix it here: minor findings about lines the task's own branch added or changed are fixed before the merge, in one fix pass. The builder gets only that list; the re-check looks only at those fixes; a blocking problem stays the only reason a review fails; anything still open after the one pass is recorded in the review file and creates no task. (c) A builder that needs a protected path its task may not edit does not propose a task: the task parks with that question, as the park list already says. (d) checks.py unmerged sorts a finding by the lines the branch changed against its fork point, not by whole file. (e) A hook of the same kind as the push hook: while a run is active it refuses a Bash command that merges a task branch unless checks.py protected, owner, review, advice and merge-limit pass for that task. (f) The advisor's job (d) changes from writing to reviewing. The manager drafts the fields of a Proposed task; the advisor rules on the draft: can each pass line be checked, does each trace back to a finding or a result, and is anything in it new scope, which it names and does not add. FROM TASK 62: a distinct exit code for checks.py consult when the task file is missing; SKILL.md says consult re-runs the paid claude-api check; LINE_NUMBER does not count a (n) after an abbreviation; a step that turns the advisor's blind labels (job a) into a labels file and runs the comparison command the line names, so a line like task 56 line 3 can be the advisor's. FROM TASK 59: the points in its item, and its note on comparing a task file with the copy at the fork point. FROM TASKS 64 AND 65: the advisor's drafted pass lines, as named in done_means below. THE SPENDING HOOK (owner, 2026-11-19: yes): while a run is active the hook refuses `claude -p` and `ant` unless the task's outside_needs names claude-api, as lines (1) and (2) of task 064's done_means describe; the task 61 builder spent about 0.59 USD with no need declared. NOT IN THIS TASK: the owner's own commit in the main folder during a run still ends the run; he has said that is good as it is. Do not change it.
done_means: (1) SKILL.md, commands/manage.md and agents/builder.md state rules (a), (b) and (c) of the notes, and a test shows a task branch that adds a Proposed task is refused unless that task's file says which earlier file and problem outside the change it is about. (2) commands/manage.md has the one fix pass of rule (b) as a step between the review and the merge, with the three limits named in the notes; the retry brief for it quotes only the minor findings. (3) checks.py unmerged decides by changed lines: tests cover a finding on lines the branch added to a file that exists on the working branch (goes to the task) and a finding on untouched lines of that file (does not). (4) While a run is active the hook refuses the merge of a task branch when any of the five merge-time checks fails for that task and allows it when all pass; tests cover both, and the hook entry in SKILL.md says what it misses. (5) agents/advisor.md, SKILL.md rule 7 and commands/manage.md describe job (d) as a review of the manager's draft, with rulings HOLDS or FAILS and a list of anything that is new scope; no text still tells the advisor to draft fields. (6) The four points taken from task 62 in the notes hold, each with a test where a script is involved. (7) The points of task 59's item hold, each with a test where a script is involved. (8) Lines (1) to (7) of the done_means in tasks/064.json hold as written there. (9) Lines (1) to (5) of the done_means in tasks/065.json hold as written there. (10) The manager tests pass, all of them, and tasks.py lint passes.
draft_note: Drafted by Claude in chat on 2026-11-17 on the owner's yes to one loose-ends task and to the one-case rule, and on his statement that the advisor should review and not write. Task 65 appeared after his yes and is folded in on the same reasoning; say so if it should stand alone. Lines (8) and (9) point at the advisor's drafts in the dropped tasks' files so nothing is retyped. The spending hook added and the task set to Ready on 2026-11-19 on the owner's instruction ("hook yes").
